note: A fixed pivot body and a sphere 2 m away on the horizontal, joined by a BallJoint at the pivot. The sphere swings under gravity and stays 2 m from the pivot, and a sideways kick (3 m/s along z) takes it out of the plane, which a ball joint allows. forceOutput names the anchor outputs raised. three.js bridge copy of the shared spec (same .x3d, same assertions): the one settle is 0.6 s where the shared spec waits 1.5 s. Measured 27 Nov 2026 in both engines (X_ITE 16.6.0 and this body, Chromium 158 SwiftShader), the ball is back at the pivot height at about 1.5 s (y 5.00 here, 4.92 in X_ITE, against the line y < 4.9) and crosses z = 0 at about 1.0 s (against |z| > 0.3), so the shared wait asks its questions at the two moments the answers flip, and X_ITE itself failed one run in three. At 0.5 to 0.75 s both engines are well inside every bound (y 3.2 to 3.9, |z| 0.78 to 1.23).
gaps: the bridge solves joints as velocity rows with a 0.2 per step error correction; a long chain of joints needs more iterations
anchor outputs are local to each body, as in X_ITE; changing anchorPoint after load does not move the joint (it is fixed from the initial poses)
forceOutput ALL raises every output of the node
